Therefore, you must always return a legal move string. # Required API The provided python file must implement the following API: ```python def policy(you: np.ndarray, opponent: np.ndarray) -> str: ... ``` # State Representation - You are always the player to move when `policy` is called. - `you` and `opponent` are 8x8 numpy arrays containing only 0/1 integers. - `you[r][c] == 1` means your disc is at row `r`, col `c`. - `opponent[r][c] == 1` means the opponent disc is at row `r`, col `c`. - An empty cell means `you[r][c] == 0` and `opponent[r][c] == 0`. - Positions are valid: never `you[r][c] == opponent[r][c] == 1`. - Move coordinates use algebraic notation: columns `a..h` map to `c = 0..7`, rows `1..8` map to `r = 0..7`.
